feature: Audit pictures show the window as a person sees it in front
summary: Pictures a walk takes now show switches, blue buttons, picked segments and traffic lights in their accent colours, matching a picture of the same window in front, while the probe still never takes your keys or your front window.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walks: a short measuring walk (the settings screenshot with the measure tool, then Settings) run three ways: with "behindLook" (the old picture), as a plain walk (now), and with "front": true (the window really in front). Also a-video-clip-fades-walk for a recording's window.

try.do: Compare the three rows: before, now, and the window really in front.
Look at Settings as a walk photographs it now: Open at login's switch is blue and the traffic lights are coloured.
Look at the editor with the measure tool: both Snap pickers show Edges and centers picked in blue.
Compare it with the same walk's old picture, where those segments are grey.
Look at a recording's window from a walk: traffic lights and the Opacity slider take the accent colour.
Keep typing in another app while a walk runs: your keys and front window stay yours.

evaluate: Do the walk pictures now look like the app does when you use it?
Is there any control still grey in a picture that is coloured when you use the app?
Is it fine that the View | Edit chip stays grey? It is grey in front too, so that is its real look.
rough: Measured: the switch track read (77,75,74) before, (56,122,244) now and (56,122,244) in front; the bar's picked Snap segment (52,55,60) before, (31,83,141) now and in front. Whole pictures: 2.17% (editor) and 0.36% (Settings) of pixels differed from in front before, 0.00% now.
A default button (the one Return presses) cannot be lent its blue: that wants the app itself in front. No such button was found in a walk picture; a walk that needs it can still say "front": true.
The check used Settings' switch, not the Agent row switch the task named, because that row only appears after a real Ask run; it is the same system switch.

Once a window is photographed it keeps the in-front look for the rest of the walk, so controls that read it (Done buttons) draw as in front from then on. Ten timing and rebuild-counting walks still pass.
This uses a private AppKit call, only in the probe build; a future macOS could drop it, and then pictures would say they show the background look again rather than fail.
